designSummary: Retrospective review of call logs; proportions with 95 percent confidence intervals and a multivariable model for delay beyond 30 minutes.
sampleSize: All critical values in two years are included, about 28,000. Precision rather than power sets the plan: a subgroup of 2,000 community results verified after 17:00 with about 70 percent notified within 30 minutes gives a 95 percent confidence interval of about plus or minus 2 percentage points. With several thousand delayed results the regression is not limited by events; parsimony comes from fixing six factors in advance.
primaryAnalysis: Proportion notified within 30 minutes overall and by location and time block, with 95 percent confidence intervals; mixed-effects logistic regression for delay beyond 30 minutes with location, time block, weekday or weekend, analyte group, night staffing and month as fixed effects and ordering clinic or ward as a random intercept.
secondaryAnalysis: Never-notified results by location and time block; median and 90th percentile time to read-back; delays by number of call attempts, reported descriptively because attempts lie on the path between location and delay.
missingData: A missing read-back time counts as not within 30 minutes in the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis excludes such calls; the share of missing times is reported by subgroup.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; subgroup estimates are reported with confidence intervals and without significance claims.
software: R; extraction query and analysis code archived with the REB file.
overfittingGuards: Call attempts not entered as a covariate in the primary model
summary: About 28,000 values; precision within about 2 points for key subgroups; mixed-effects logistic model with six pre-specified factors.
